result:
I’m just going to say it: the world is unreasonably, almost offensively beautiful sometimes.

This morning I watched the sun come up over the city and it looked like the sky had decided to set itself on fire just to say “good morning.” Pink turning into gold turning into that impossible blue that makes you feel like a kid again. And for a few quiet minutes the whole messy, loud, broken planet just… paused. No notifications. No opinions. Just light doing what light has done for four billion years, completely unbothered by our dramas.

I’ve been thinking a lot lately about how most of the things that actually matter can’t be bought, optimized, or posted about. The way someone’s laugh sounds when they’re not trying to impress anyone. The smell of rain on hot pavement. How it feels when a song you forgot you loved suddenly finds you again at 2 a.m. and cracks your chest open in the best way. These tiny, stupid, perfect moments that don’t scale and can’t be monetized.

We’re all running around collecting experiences like they’re Pokémon, but I’m starting to believe the real flex is the opposite: the ability to be completely here, right now, without needing to document it or turn it into content. Just… witnessing. Feeling the full weight and ridiculousness of being alive.

I don’t know. Maybe I’m getting soft in my old age (I’m 31, practically ancient). But I keep catching myself tearing up at the smallest things lately. A perfectly ripe peach. My dog dreaming and making those little running noises. The fact that humans invented music at all. That we looked at the void and decided to sing into it.

Anyway. I hope you’re having a day that feels like it belongs to you. That somewhere in it you find one of those stupid little perfect moments and let yourself be stupidly, perfectly moved by it.

The world is loud. Don’t let it make you hard. Stay soft. It’s a revolutionary act.
